meta.title: Grade 9 Olympiad & Foundation Physics Universal Topic Adapter & Subtopic Competency Framework
meta.description: Unified curriculum contract binding Core 1A Conceptual Ontologies, Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstructions, Core 2 QRT Question Banks, and Multi-Engine Automated Validation Gates.

common_framework.description: Universal physical invariants, pedagogical contracts, and verification gates shared across all physics topics.

stage_1_choose.name: System Demarcation & Frame Selection
invariants: Explicitly identify the physical body or closed multi-body system boundary.
Select reference frame (inertial ground frame vs accelerated non-inertial frame with explicit D'Alembert pseudo-forces).
Declare coordinate origin, positive axis orientation, and shared clock baseline (t = 0).
Register explicit model assumptions and idealizations before applying formulas.

stage_2_represent.name: Representation Construction
invariants: Translate physical story into an exact scientific representation before algebraic computation.
Allowed representation forms: Free-Body Diagram (FBD), Interaction Map, Coordinate/Trajectory Graph, Potential Well Curve, State Table, or Momentum Vector Triangle.
Typography floor: Every SVG diagram must declare text font-size >= 14px on all labels, coordinates, and annotations.
Visual integrity: Force vectors must originate at point of application/COM; action-reaction pairs must NEVER appear on the same isolated body.

stage_3_connect.name: Law Connection & Governing Constraints
invariants: Connect representation to the fundamental physical invariant law, never by guessing a formula name.
State explicit scope conditions: identify where the model holds and where it breaks (e.g. h << R_E, v << c, static slip threshold f_s <= mu_s * N, incompressible fluid).
Identify kinematic constraints: string inextensibility, rigid contact, shared time across orthogonal components.

stage_4_execute_and_check.name: Execution & Multi-Engine Physical Verification
invariants: Execute algebra step-by-step without skipping intermediate learner operations.
Sanity Check: Direction and sign must match physical reality.
Dimensional Homogeneity: Verify base SI dimensional powers [M]^a [L]^b [T]^c [Theta]^d.
Dual Limiting Extremals: Stress-test at least 2 independent boundary conditions (e.g. zero mass, infinite distance, right angle, zero friction).
Cross-Core Recovery Anchor: Every distractor trap and reasoning step must link to an explicit numbered Core 1 atomic competency.

universal_pedagogical_contract.attempt_protection: Questions must protect answers, reveals, and derivations until a learner attempt is committed.

hint_ladder_protocol.tier_1: H1 - What is the key physics? Open prompt question probing the decisive event, state, or invariant, followed by an expandable reveal.
hint_ladder_protocol.tier_2: H2 - How would you represent it? Open prompt question probing coordinate axes, FBD, or state diagram, followed by an expandable reveal.
hint_ladder_protocol.tier_3: H3 - What would you write first? Open prompt question probing the first executable constraint equation, followed by an expandable reveal.

reasoning_ladder_protocol.step_1_understand: Identify body, physical event, and given states.
reasoning_ladder_protocol.step_2_represent: Establish coordinate axes, FBD, or boundary sketch.
reasoning_ladder_protocol.step_4_calculate: Execute algebraic manipulation without unstated jumps.

tripartite_verification_protocol.check_it_another_way: Independent boundary limit or alternative model verification.
tripartite_verification_protocol.watch_out: Explicit warning against the authentic misconception trap.
tripartite_verification_protocol.review_this_idea: Direct Cross-Core 1-to-1 link citing exact competency ID.

universal_verification_gates: Gate 1: Math & Typography (0 unrendered raw TeX blocks outside scripts; valid KaTeX syntax)
Gate 2: Vector & Diagram Typography Floor (All SVG text font-size >= 14px)
Gate 3: Dimensional Homogeneity (Base SI dimensions verified)
Gate 4: Dual Limiting Extremals (>= 2 falsifiable boundary limits declared)
Gate 5: Distractor Disjointness & Authentic Trap Binding (4 pairwise disjoint options with genuine diagnostic types)
Gate 6: Subtopic Competency 1-to-1 Coverage (Every question bound to an explicit subtopic competency code)
Gate 7: Static DOM Pre-Rendered KaTeX & 48px Touch Target Floor (Full static HTML DOM with min-height: 48px touch targets)

mechanics-nlm.display_name: Newton's Laws of Motion & Momentum Systems

coordinate_conventions.system: 1D/2D Cartesian with origin at chosen body center of mass
coordinate_conventions.axes: x-axis along line of motion or inclined surface, y-axis perpendicular to surface
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Direction of anticipated acceleration chosen as positive axis (+x) to eliminate extraneous negative signs
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Mass in kg, Force in N = kg m s^-2, Acceleration in m s^-2, Momentum in kg m s^-1, Time in s)

svg_specifications: Body isolated from environment with center-of-mass origin
Force arrows begin at point of contact or COM and point along direction of push/pull
Newton III action-reaction pairs must NEVER appear on the same isolated body
Friction vector strictly tangential to contact plane; normal force strictly perpendicular
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all force labels, masses, and angles

NLM-01.title: Motion is not Force
NLM-01.subtitle: Constant velocity can coexist with zero net force
NLM-01.canonical_rule: Constant velocity can coexist with zero net force; net force determines acceleration (rate of change of velocity), not velocity itself.
NLM-01.model_check: Distinguish between zero net force (Sigma F = 0) and absence of individual physical interactions.
subtopics: Zero net force coexisting with constant velocity
Distinction between zero net force and absence of forces
Inertial reference frames and the principle of inertia
Inertia during sudden braking (passenger lurch without fictitious forward force)
Coin tossed vertically in an accelerating train (horizontal velocity retention)
Fluid inertia in decelerating tankers (liquid surge toward front)
Motion on ideal frictionless surfaces requiring zero sustaining force
NLM-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming an object moving forward must have a net forward force pushing it.

NLM-02.title: Choose the Body Before Drawing Forces
NLM-02.subtitle: Interactions become forces only after the body is chosen
NLM-02.canonical_rule: Interactions become forces only after the target body is chosen; only external forces acting ON the chosen body enter Sigma F = ma.
NLM-02.scope_condition: Closed system boundary demarcating internal from external interactions.
NLM-02.model_check: Never include forces that the chosen body exerts ON other objects.
subtopics: Closed system boundary demarcation
Interaction mapping: identifying contact vs non-contact external agents
Naming convention: 'force on X by Y'
Eliminating body confusion (never placing forces exerted BY the body on its own FBD)
FBD construction for isolated bodies
Ideal frictionless surfaces: normal contact force only, zero shear and zero rolling torque
NLM-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Drawing forces exerted BY the body onto its own Free-Body Diagram.

NLM-03.title: Net Force is a Vector Sum
NLM-03.subtitle: Balanced forces and no forces are different statements
NLM-03.canonical_rule: Forces add vectorially, not algebraically; balanced forces produce zero acceleration along each orthogonal axis independently.
NLM-03.scope_condition: Orthogonal Cartesian coordinate decomposition (Sigma F_x = m a_x, Sigma F_y = m a_y).
NLM-03.model_check: Decompose all diagonal forces into rectangular components before summing.
subtopics: Collinear vector addition with explicit signed components
Orthogonal Cartesian force decomposition (Sigma F_x = m a_x, Sigma F_y = m a_y)
Dynamic equilibrium at constant velocity (horse pulling cart at constant speed)
Distinguishing balanced forces from absence of forces
Mass as the quantitative measure of translational inertia
Ranking inertia across equal-volume or differing-mass objects
NLM-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Adding vector magnitudes directly without trigonometric component resolution.

NLM-04.title: Newton II and Scaling
NLM-04.subtitle: Acceleration responds to net force and mass together
NLM-04.canonical_rule: Acceleration is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to total mass: a = Sigma F_ext / M_tot.
NLM-04.scope_condition: Constant mass systems (non-relativistic, non-rocket mass shedding).
NLM-04.model_check: When bodies move with common acceleration, treat the coupled assembly as a single composite system.
subtopics: Fundamental dynamic equation: F_net = ma
Force and mass scaling ratios: a2/a1 = (F2/F1)(m1/m2)
Coupled masses under the same external force: a_tot = (a1 * a2)/(a1 + a2)
Single-body vs multi-body composite system acceleration
Atwood machine coupled acceleration and string tension harmonic mean
NLM-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Using individual applied force instead of vector net force in a = F/m.

NLM-05.title: Stopping Force Needs Two Models
NLM-05.subtitle: Kinematics supplies acceleration; Newton II supplies force
NLM-05.canonical_rule: Determining stopping force requires coupling kinematics with dynamics: kinematics supplies acceleration; Newton II supplies retarding force.
NLM-05.scope_condition: Uniform stopping acceleration over displacement s or duration t.
NLM-05.model_check: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as or v = u + at to isolate a, then evaluate F_stop = m|a|.
subtopics: Two-stage model coupling: Kinematics <-> Dynamics
Stopping over distance s: v^2 = u^2 + 2as => a = -u^2/(2s)
Stopping force calculation: F_stop = m|a| = mu^2/(2s)
Stopping duration: v = u + at => t = u/|a| = 2s/u
Quadratic velocity scaling of stopping force
NLM-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Attempting to calculate stopping force without determining acceleration or time.

NLM-06.title: Momentum is a Signed State
NLM-06.subtitle: Momentum carries the direction of velocity
NLM-06.canonical_rule: Momentum p = m * v is a directional vector carrying the sign of velocity; reversing direction produces Delta p = -m(v1 + v2), not zero.
NLM-06.model_check: Always establish a positive axis before assigning signs to momentum states.
subtopics: Linear momentum as signed vector quantity: p = mv
1D coordinate sign assignment (+p and -p)
Rebound dynamics: reversal of velocity producing large Delta p
Directional momentum change vs scalar speed difference
Momentum-velocity (p-v) graph slope as mass m
Momentum-mass (p-m) graph slope as velocity v
NLM-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Subtracting momentum magnitudes without accounting for opposite directional signs.

NLM-07.title: Impulse and Average Force
NLM-07.subtitle: The same momentum change can be spread over more time
NLM-07.canonical_rule: Impulse J = Delta p = F_avg * Delta t; spreading a fixed momentum change over a longer time interval reduces the peak contact force.
NLM-07.model_check: Area under F-t curve equals total momentum change Delta p.
subtopics: Impulse-momentum theorem: J = Delta p = F_avg * Delta t
Impact duration tradeoff: extending Delta t reduces average force
Catching mechanics: cushioning impact by moving hands backward
Force-time (F-t) graph: area under curve equals total impulse Delta p
Distinguishing impulse (N*s) from work (J) and momentum from force
NLM-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing impulse (change in momentum in N*s) with work done (energy transferred in Joules).

NLM-08.title: Newton III Pairs
NLM-08.subtitle: Equal and opposite does not mean same body
NLM-08.canonical_rule: Every interaction between two bodies consists of equal and opposite forces acting simultaneously on different bodies: F_12 = -F_21.
NLM-08.scope_condition: Universal interaction law valid across all mass ratios and contact/field interfaces.
NLM-08.model_check: Because action and reaction act on strictly different bodies, they NEVER cancel each other out on an individual body's FBD.
subtopics: Third-law reciprocal action-reaction pairs: F_AB = -F_BA
Forces acting on strictly different bodies: never cancelling on one body's FBD
Normal force vs weight distinction on a resting body (balanced forces on one body vs 3rd law pair)
Wall push reaction force
Horse and cart paradox resolution via ground friction on horse hooves
Sprinkler rotational reaction via backward fluid ejection
NLM-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing a massive object exerts a greater gravitational or contact force than a lighter object.

NLM-09.title: Momentum Conservation is a System Statement
NLM-09.subtitle: Choose the system and check external impulse first
NLM-09.canonical_rule: In the absence of net external impulse (Sigma F_ext = 0), the total momentum of a multi-body system is strictly conserved: P_total = const.
NLM-09.scope_condition: Isolated multi-body systems; internal interaction forces cancel identically by Newton III.
NLM-09.model_check: Choose the system boundary large enough that all explosive or collision forces become internal.
subtopics: System boundary demarcation and internal force cancellation
External impulse verification condition: Sigma F_ext = 0
Why a falling ball alone does not conserve momentum (external gravity impulse)
Why the ball + Earth system conserves total momentum
Separation from rest: P_initial = 0 => m1*v1 + m2*v2 = 0
Two skaters pushing apart on frictionless ice
NLM-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Applying momentum conservation to an isolated single body under external gravity.

NLM-10.title: Recoil, Rockets and Exchanged Momentum
NLM-10.subtitle: Equal momentum can mean very different speeds
NLM-10.canonical_rule: In recoil and separation events, internal momentum exchange produces equal and opposite momenta, with speeds scaling inversely with mass.
NLM-10.scope_condition: Isolated explosive or recoil events; rocket mass expulsion.
NLM-10.model_check: For equal momentum magnitude, speed and kinetic energy scale inversely with mass (v proportional to 1/m, K proportional to 1/m).
subtopics: Recoil dynamics in isolated systems: m_bullet * v_bullet = m_gun * v_recoil
Inverse speed-mass scaling: v proportional to 1/m for equal momentum
Kinetic energy partitioning: K = p^2/(2m) proportional to 1/m (lighter object carries most kinetic energy)
Rocket propulsion in deep space via backward exhaust ejection
Thrust via continuous mass ejection rate: F_thrust = v_rel * (dm/dt)
NLM-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming equal momentum implies equal speed or equal kinetic energy.

NLM-11.title: Read Force from a Motion Graph
NLM-11.subtitle: v-t slope -> acceleration -> force
NLM-11.canonical_rule: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration (dv/dt), which multiplied by mass yields net force: F_net = m * (dv/dt).
NLM-11.model_check: Zero slope indicates zero net force; constant non-zero slope indicates constant net force; sign of slope dictates force direction.
subtopics: Velocity-time graph slope as acceleration: a = Delta v / Delta t
Net force deduction: F_net = m * slope
Frictional retarding force deduction from deceleration slope
Segmented piecewise velocity-time profiles
Avoiding area misinterpretation (area under v-t is displacement, not force)
NLM-11.easy_mistake_to_make: Inferring force from the height of the velocity curve rather than its slope.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing a net force is needed to maintain constant velocity; confusing v = const with F_net > 0.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Newton's 1st Law: Net force determines acceleration (rate of change of velocity), not velocity itself.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing action and reaction cancel each other out on the same body.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Newton's 3rd Law pairs act on strictly distinct interacting bodies: F_AB = -F_BA.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming normal force N always equals mg, regardless of incline, vertical acceleration, or applied external forces.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Normal force is a self-adjusting constraint force determined by equilibrium/acceleration along the perpendicular axis: Sigma F_perp = m a_perp.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming static friction always equals mu_s * N even when external applied force is smaller.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Static friction is self-adjusting: 0 <= f_s <= mu_s * N; it exactly matches applied driving force until slip threshold.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing friction always opposes the velocity of the body in the lab frame.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Friction opposes relative sliding between surfaces in contact, not absolute motion in the lab frame (e.g. walking, car driving, stacked block accelerating).

coordinate_conventions.axes: x-axis horizontal along launch direction (+x rightward), y-axis vertical (+y upward, so a_y = -g)
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Upward positive, rightward positive. Gravity acceleration vector is strictly a = -g j.
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Position in m, Velocity in m s^-1, Acceleration in m s^-2, Time in s, Angle in radians/degrees)

svg_specifications: Coordinate axes labeled with variable and unit: x (m), y (m), v (m/s), t (s)
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all axis labels, coordinate values, and annotations
Key landmark points (apex, half-height, impact, graph intercepts) marked with distinct circles (r >= 4)
In projectile diagrams, initial launch vector u must show resolved components u_x and u_y with dashed projection lines

KIN-01.title: Distance vs Displacement Invariant
KIN-01.canonical_rule: Distance is the scalar cumulative path length; displacement is the vector difference between final and initial positions: Delta r = r_final - r_initial.
KIN-01.model_check: Distance equals magnitude of displacement IF AND ONLY IF motion is along a straight line without reversal.
KIN-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Equating distance with displacement magnitude when motion reverses direction.

KIN-02.title: Average Speed vs Average Velocity
KIN-02.canonical_rule: Average speed is total distance divided by total elapsed time; average velocity is total vector displacement divided by total time: v_avg = Delta r / Delta t.
KIN-02.model_check: For closed round trips, average velocity is identically zero, whereas average speed is strictly positive.
KIN-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Calculating average speed by averaging initial and final velocities in non-uniformly accelerated motion.

KIN-03.title: Weighted Kinematic Averages
KIN-03.canonical_rule: Equal-time intervals yield arithmetic mean v_avg = (v1 + v2)/2; equal-distance intervals yield harmonic mean v_avg = 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2).
KIN-03.model_check: Never use arithmetic mean when equal distances are covered at different speeds.
KIN-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Using arithmetic average for equal distance segments.

KIN-04.title: Signs, Direction & Acceleration Reversal
KIN-04.canonical_rule: Sign of velocity indicates direction of motion; sign of acceleration indicates direction of velocity change; negative acceleration speeds up a body moving in the negative direction.
KIN-04.model_check: Speeding up occurs when v and a have identical signs; slowing down occurs when v and a have opposing signs.
KIN-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming negative acceleration always means slowing down (deceleration).

KIN-05.title: Constant Acceleration Equation Selection
KIN-05.canonical_rule: The kinematic quad (v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2, v^2 = u^2 + 2as, s = (u+v)/2 * t) is valid IF AND ONLY IF acceleration is constant.
KIN-05.model_check: Select the single kinematic equation that eliminates the unmeasured/unrequested parameter.
KIN-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Applying constant-acceleration equations to non-uniform or variable-acceleration motion.

KIN-06.title: Multiphase & Delayed-Start Motion
KIN-06.canonical_rule: Complex motions must be partitioned into piecewise uniform acceleration intervals, matching final state of phase 1 to initial state of phase 2.
KIN-06.model_check: For delayed start, adjust time coordinate: t_B = t_A - Delta t.
KIN-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Using a single global equation across multiple acceleration regimes.

KIN-07.title: Vertical Free Fall & Apex Invariants
KIN-07.canonical_rule: Under gravity, acceleration is strictly a_y = -g throughout flight; at apex, vertical velocity vanishes (v_y = 0) while acceleration remains exactly -g.
KIN-07.model_check: Time of ascent equals time of descent to the same horizontal level: t_up = t_down = u/g.
KIN-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming acceleration is zero at the highest point (apex) of flight.

KIN-08.title: 2D Projectile Component Decoupling
KIN-08.canonical_rule: Perpendicular motions are completely independent and share only a single common parameter: elapsed time t.
KIN-08.model_check: Horizontal velocity u_x = u cos theta remains constant; vertical motion is free fall u_y = u sin theta under a_y = -g.
KIN-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing horizontal velocity influences vertical flight time or rate of vertical fall.

KIN-09.title: Projectile Trajectory & Flight Landmarks
KIN-09.canonical_rule: Trajectory is a parabola y(x) = x tan theta - (g / (2 u^2 cos^2 theta)) x^2; flight time T = 2u sin theta / g; range R = u^2 sin 2theta / g.
KIN-09.scope_condition: Launch and landing on horizontal plane.
KIN-09.model_check: Complementary launch angles (theta and 90 deg - theta) yield identical horizontal ranges at equal launch speeds.
KIN-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Using symmetric range formula when launch and landing heights are unequal.

KIN-10.title: Relative Velocity & Common Acceleration Cancellation
KIN-10.canonical_rule: Relative velocity is v_AB = v_A - v_B; two projectiles in the same gravity field share common acceleration (a_A = a_B = -g), so relative acceleration is ZERO.
KIN-10.model_check: Because a_rel = 0, the trajectory of one projectile as viewed from another projectile is a straight line at constant velocity.
KIN-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Adding velocities algebraically without vector subtraction.

KIN-11.title: Motion Graphs & Geometric Calculus
KIN-11.canonical_rule: Slope of position graph is velocity; slope of velocity graph is acceleration; area under velocity-time graph is displacement; area under acceleration-time graph is change in velocity.
KIN-11.model_check: Sharp corners on x-t graphs imply infinite acceleration (physically impossible in finite force regimes).
KIN-11.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing position graph height with velocity, or negative velocity with deceleration.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming instantaneous zero velocity at apex implies zero acceleration.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Acceleration is rate of velocity change (dv/dt = -g), not velocity. Zero acceleration would mean the particle stops and hovers.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Equating total distance with magnitude of displacement when direction reverses.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Distance is cumulative path length; displacement is net position difference r_final - r_initial.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Calculating average speed as arithmetic average (v1 + v2)/2 for equal distance segments.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Average speed is total distance over total time, yielding harmonic mean 2*v1*v2 / (v1 + v2).

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing horizontal launch speed extends vertical flight time compared to pure drop.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Orthogonal motions are decoupled. Vertical acceleration is -g regardless of horizontal velocity.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Confusing position graph height with velocity, or negative velocity with deceleration.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Velocity is the slope dx/dt, not position coordinate x. Negative velocity with positive slope represents slowing down in the reverse direction.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Claiming constant speed in circular motion implies zero acceleration.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Velocity vector turns continuously, requiring inward normal centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2/r.

work-energy-power.display_name: Work, Energy & Power: Conservative Fields & Potential Wells

coordinate_conventions.system: 1D/2D Cartesian with declared potential energy datum U = 0
coordinate_conventions.axes: x-axis along displacement direction; vertical elevation y-axis upward for gravity
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Work is positive when force has an acute component along displacement (cos theta > 0). Potential energy increases against the conservative force (dU = -F_c dx).
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Work & Energy in Joules = N m = kg m^2 s^-2, Power in Watts = J s^-1 = kg m^2 s^-3, Spring constant in N m^-1 = kg s^-2)

svg_specifications: Coordinate axes labeled with variable and unit: x (m), F (N), U (J), K (J), P (W)
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all axis labels, coordinate values, and annotations
Potential energy curves U(x) must show total mechanical energy line E and turning points where E = U(x)
Force-displacement graphs must distinguish positive area above axis from negative area below axis

WEP-01.title: Definition of Mechanical Work
WEP-01.canonical_rule: Work by a constant force is the scalar product W = F * d * cos theta; perpendicular forces (cos 90 deg = 0) perform identically zero work.
WEP-01.model_check: Centripetal force is strictly perpendicular to velocity (F_c perp v), doing zero work and keeping kinetic energy constant.
WEP-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming centripetal force does work because it redirects the path.

WEP-02.title: Work by Variable Forces & Spring Integration
WEP-02.canonical_rule: Work by a variable force equals the integral W = int F(x) dx (area under F-x curve); Hookean spring work is W = 1/2 k x^2.
WEP-02.model_check: Spring force increases linearly from 0 to kx, so average force is 1/2 kx, producing triangular area 1/2 kx^2.
WEP-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Multiplying maximum spring force by displacement: W = F_max * x = kx^2.

WEP-03.title: Work-Energy Theorem
WEP-03.canonical_rule: The net work done by ALL forces acting on a body equals its change in kinetic energy: W_net = Delta K = 1/2 m v_f^2 - 1/2 m v_i^2.
WEP-03.scope_condition: Valid in any inertial reference frame across both conservative and non-conservative forces.
WEP-03.model_check: W_net includes conservative forces, non-conservative friction, and external applied forces.
WEP-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Equating work done by a single force to total change in kinetic energy when other forces act.

WEP-04.title: Conservative Forces & Path Independence
WEP-04.canonical_rule: A force is conservative if work done around any closed loop is zero (oint F . dr = 0), or equivalently, work between two points is path-independent.
WEP-04.scope_condition: Conservative vector fields (gravity, ideal spring, electrostatic).
WEP-04.model_check: Non-conservative forces (kinetic friction, air drag) dissipate mechanical energy into heat; work depends on actual path length.

WEP-05.title: Gravitational & Elastic Potential Energy Wells
WEP-05.canonical_rule: Potential energy is defined only for conservative forces via Delta U = -W_c; near Earth U = mgh; for springs U = 1/2 kx^2.
WEP-05.model_check: Only potential energy differences Delta U have physical meaning; absolute value depends on chosen arbitrary datum.
WEP-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Treating potential energy as having an absolute intrinsic value without datum definition.

WEP-06.title: Conservative Force as Negative Potential Gradient
WEP-06.canonical_rule: In 1D, conservative force is the negative derivative of potential energy: F(x) = -dU/dx; equilibrium occurs where dU/dx = 0.
WEP-06.model_check: Stable equilibrium: d^2U/dx^2 > 0 (potential minimum); Unstable equilibrium: d^2U/dx^2 < 0 (potential maximum).
WEP-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Equating force directly to potential energy U(x) instead of its negative spatial derivative.

WEP-07.title: Mechanical Energy Conservation & Turning Points
WEP-07.canonical_rule: In an isolated system with only conservative forces, total mechanical energy is conserved: E = K + U = const.
WEP-07.model_check: Motion is bounded in regions where E >= U(x); turning points occur where E = U(x) and kinetic energy vanishes (K = 0).
WEP-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming energy is conserved when non-conservative friction is active.

WEP-08.title: Power as Rate of Energy Transfer
WEP-08.canonical_rule: Instantaneous power is P = dW/dt = F . v; average power is P_avg = W_total / Delta t.
WEP-08.model_check: Distinguish between total work in Joules and delivery rate in Watts: a low-power engine running long can do more total work than a high-power engine running briefly.

WEP-09.title: Non-Holonomic Friction Work in Multi-Body Systems
WEP-09.canonical_rule: Kinetic friction does negative work on total system mechanical energy, but can do POSITIVE work on an individual accelerating component body.
WEP-09.model_check: A box placed on a moving conveyor belt accelerates due to forward kinetic friction, which does positive work on the box in the lab frame.
WEP-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing friction can never do positive work on any individual body.

WEP-10.title: Momentum vs Kinetic Energy Scaling
WEP-10.canonical_rule: Kinetic energy relates to momentum via K = p^2 / (2m); for equal momentum, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass.
WEP-10.model_check: When a gun fires a bullet, gun and bullet have equal and opposite momentum (p_g = p_b), but the light bullet carries vastly greater kinetic energy.
WEP-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming two objects with equal momentum must carry equal kinetic energy.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing centripetal force does work because it continuously redirects the body.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Centripetal force is strictly perpendicular to velocity (F_c perp v => F_c . dr = 0), doing zero work and leaving kinetic energy unchanged.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Treating potential energy as having an absolute intrinsic value without datum definition.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Potential energy is physically meaningful only through differences Delta U = -W_c. The zero level U = 0 is an arbitrary coordinate convention.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Confusing total energy transferred (work in Joules) with rate of transfer (power in Watts).
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Power is dW/dt. A low-power machine running for a long duration can do vastly more total work than a high-power machine running for a microsecond.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming spring work equals F_max * x = kx^2 instead of 0.5*k*x^2.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Spring force varies linearly from 0 to kx. The work integral is int_0^x kx' dx' = 0.5 * k * x^2 (half the bounding rectangle).

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing friction can never do positive work on any individual body.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Kinetic friction does positive work on a body that it accelerates forward (e.g. box placed on moving conveyor belt, top block on moving cart).

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming two objects with equal momentum must possess equal kinetic energy.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: K = p^2 / (2m). For equal momentum, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass; the lighter object carries vastly greater kinetic energy.

gravitation-orbital-motion.display_name: Universal Gravitation, Kepler's Laws & Orbital Mechanics

coordinate_conventions.system: Spherical / Polar coordinates (r, theta) centered at primary body center of mass
coordinate_conventions.datum: Gravitational potential datum strictly at infinity: U(r -> infinity) = 0, so U(r) = -G M m / r is universally negative for bound systems
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Radial unit vector r_hat points outward from center; gravitational force is strictly attractive: F_g = - (G M m / r^2) r_hat
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Distance in m, Mass in kg, Gravitational constant G in N m^2 kg^-2 = m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, Field in m s^-2, Potential in J kg^-1 = m^2 s^-2)

svg_specifications: Coordinate axes labeled: r (m), g (m/s^2), U (J), v (m/s)
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all labels and annotations
Primary central mass, orbiting satellite/planet, and focal points clearly distinguished
Inside vs outside Earth field profiles clearly marked with boundary at r = R

GRAV-01.title: Newton's Universal Inverse-Square Law
GRAV-01.canonical_rule: Every point mass attracts every other point mass with force F = G * m1 * m2 / r^2; Third law pairing |F_12| = |F_21| holds regardless of mass disparity.
GRAV-01.scope_condition: Point masses and spherically symmetric mass distributions in non-relativistic regimes.
GRAV-01.model_check: Earth attracts an apple with the exact same force magnitude that the apple attracts the Earth.
GRAV-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming a massive planet exerts a greater gravitational force than a smaller attracted object.

GRAV-02.title: Surface Gravity & Proportional Scaling
GRAV-02.canonical_rule: Acceleration due to gravity at surface is g_0 = GM/R^2 = 4/3 pi G rho R; scaling depends on mass over radius squared.
GRAV-02.scope_condition: Spherical celestial bodies with uniform or radially symmetric density rho(r).
GRAV-02.model_check: Doubling mass and doubling radius halves surface gravity: 2 / 2^2 = 1/2.
GRAV-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Scaling surface gravity linearly with radius or mass without squaring radius.

GRAV-03.title: Altitude Variation of Gravity
GRAV-03.canonical_rule: At altitude h above surface, exact gravity is g(h) = g_0 * (R / (R + h))^2; linear binomial approximation 1 - 2h/R holds strictly for h << R.
GRAV-03.model_check: At h = R, gravity is exactly 1/4 g_0; binomial approximation yields 1 - 2(1) = -1 (completely invalid).
GRAV-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Using the small-altitude linear approximation for large planetary altitudes.

GRAV-04.title: Newton's Shell Theorem & Interior Depth Field
GRAV-04.canonical_rule: A uniform spherical shell exerts zero net force inside; inside a uniform solid sphere, field decreases linearly g(d) = g_0(1 - d/R) = (GM/R^3)*r to zero at the center.
GRAV-04.model_check: Only the enclosed core mass M(r) = M*(r/R)^3 attracts; outer layers cancel to zero by solid angle symmetry.
GRAV-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming gravity increases to infinity as one descends toward Earth's center according to 1/r^2.

GRAV-05.title: Earth Tunnel Simple Harmonic Motion
GRAV-05.canonical_rule: A particle in an evacuated frictionless tunnel drilled through uniform Earth executes simple harmonic motion with period T = 2pi * sqrt(R/g_0) approx 84.6 min, invariant across all chords.
GRAV-05.scope_condition: Uniform Earth density; frictionless evacuated tunnel.
GRAV-05.model_check: Along any chord tunnel, the transverse normal force cancels, leaving F_x = -(mg_0/R)*x with identical effective stiffness k = mg_0/R.
GRAV-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming a chord tunnel has a different period because it is shorter than a diametrical tunnel.

GRAV-06.title: Gravitational Potential Energy Well
GRAV-06.canonical_rule: With datum U(infinity) = 0, gravitational potential energy is strictly negative U(r) = -GMm/r for all bound states; work to lift mass to h = R is Delta U = 1/2 mg_0 R.
GRAV-06.scope_condition: Asymptotically flat space; datum at infinity.
GRAV-06.model_check: Negative sign signifies bound state; external agent must inject positive energy to separate masses to infinity.
GRAV-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Using flat-Earth W = mgh = mg_0 R at planetary altitudes where field dilutes.

GRAV-07.title: Kepler's Second Law & Angular Momentum Conservation
GRAV-07.canonical_rule: Under central gravity, torque is zero (tau = r x F = 0), so angular momentum is conserved, ensuring constant areal velocity dA/dt = L/(2m) and speed reciprocity r_p * v_p = r_a * v_a.
GRAV-07.model_check: Orbital speed is strictly maximum at perihelion (closest) and minimum at aphelion (farthest).
GRAV-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming planets travel at uniform speed in elliptical orbits.

GRAV-08.title: Kepler's Third Law Harmonic Scaling
GRAV-08.canonical_rule: Orbital period squared is proportional to semi-major axis cubed: T^2 = (4pi^2 / GM) * a^3; ratio T_1^2 / T_2^2 = a_1^3 / a_2^3.
GRAV-08.scope_condition: Two-body Keplerian system dominated by central mass M >> m.
GRAV-08.model_check: Period scaling follows power 3/2: T proportional to r^(1.5).
GRAV-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming orbital period scales linearly with orbital radius.

GRAV-09.title: Orbital Speed, Escape Speed & Virial Theorem
GRAV-09.canonical_rule: Circular orbital velocity is v_orb = sqrt(GM/r); escape velocity is v_esc = sqrt(2) * v_orb; total energy is E = -K = 1/2 U; atmospheric drag causes inward spiral that paradoxically increases speed.
GRAV-09.model_check: Escape velocity is 41.4% higher than circular orbital velocity; escaping with residual speed yields v_inf = sqrt(v_0^2 - v_esc^2).
GRAV-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing circular orbital velocity with parabolic escape velocity.

GRAV-10.title: Multi-Body Gravity, Cavities & Tides
GRAV-10.canonical_rule: Binary stars orbit common center of mass with identical period T = 2pi*sqrt(d^3 / G(m1+m2)); field inside an off-center spherical cavity is strictly uniform g_cav = -4/3 pi G rho d; tidal acceleration scales as 1/d^3 producing two daily bulges.
GRAV-10.scope_condition: Multi-body configurations and differential field gradients.
GRAV-10.model_check: Tides are differential (dg/dd proportional to 1/d^3), pulling near water toward Moon and pulling Earth away from far water, creating two symmetric bulges.
GRAV-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing tides pull only on the near side of Earth or that cavity field is non-uniform.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing astronauts in orbit experience zero gravity because gravity does not reach space.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Gravity at 400 km ISS orbit is still ~8.8 m/s^2 (~90% of surface g). Weightlessness is free-fall apparent weightlessness where normal contact force N = 0.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming gravity increases without bound as one descends toward the Earth's center according to 1/r^2.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: By Newton's Shell Theorem, only mass enclosed within radius r contributes; field decreases linearly g(r) = (GM/R^3)*r to zero at the center.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Confusing circular orbital velocity v_orb = sqrt(GM/r) with parabolic escape velocity v_esc = sqrt(2GM/r).
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Escape velocity is larger by factor sqrt(2) approx 1.414; orbital velocity yields a bound closed circular orbit, whereas escape velocity permanently unbinds the body to r -> infinity with zero residual speed.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming planets travel at uniform speed in elliptical orbits.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: By Kepler's 2nd Law (conservation of angular momentum L = m r v_perp), areal velocity is constant, so linear speed is maximum at perihelion and minimum at aphelion.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing the Moon attracts water only on the near side of Earth, producing a single daily tidal bulge.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Differential gravitational tidal gradient pulls near water more than solid Earth, and pulls solid Earth more than far water, producing two symmetric tidal bulges.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Conflating invariant inertial mass m with local gravitational force W = mg.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Mass is an intrinsic scalar measure of inertia independent of location; weight is the downward gravitational force that varies with local field g.

fluids-hydrostatics.display_name: Fluids: Hydrostatics, Pascal's Principle & Archimedes' Law

coordinate_conventions.system: 1D/2D vertical depth axis h measured downward from free liquid surface, or elevation y measured upward
coordinate_conventions.pressure_nature: Scalar isotropic pressure acting perpendicular to any immersed surface: P = P_0 + rho * g * h
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Downward depth h increases hydrostatic pressure; upward normal buoyant force opposes gravity
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Pressure in Pa = N m^-2 = kg m^-1 s^-2, Density in kg m^-3, Surface tension in N m^-1 = kg s^-2, Volume in m^3)

svg_specifications: Liquid levels, interfaces, and free surfaces marked with distinct color/pattern
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all labels and annotations
Buoyant force vector F_B and weight vector W displayed with proper points of action (center of buoyancy vs center of gravity)
Hydrostatic pressure arrows against vertical walls displayed perpendicular to surface with linearly increasing magnitude

FLUID-01.title: Fluid Pressure as Isotropic Scalar
FLUID-01.canonical_rule: Pressure P = dF_perp / dA is a scalar acting isotropically with equal magnitude in all spatial directions at a given depth.
FLUID-01.model_check: Pressure force always acts strictly perpendicular to any immersed surface boundary regardless of surface orientation.
FLUID-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Treating pressure as a directional vector rather than an isotropic scalar.

FLUID-02.title: Hydrostatic Depth Law & Paradox
FLUID-02.canonical_rule: Hydrostatic pressure P(h) = P_0 + rho * g * h depends strictly on vertical column depth h and fluid density rho, completely independent of container geometry or lateral wall slope.
FLUID-02.model_check: Containers of different shapes with identical base areas and liquid depths experience identical bottom pressures and base forces (Hydrostatic Paradox).
FLUID-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming liquid pressure at container bottom depends on container shape or total liquid volume.

FLUID-03.title: Pascal's Principle & Hydraulic Leverage
FLUID-03.canonical_rule: Pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and container walls: Delta P_1 = Delta P_2 => F_1 / A_1 = F_2 / A_2.
FLUID-03.scope_condition: Enclosed, incompressible fluids in static equilibrium.
FLUID-03.model_check: Work done on input piston equals work done by output piston (F1 * d1 = F2 * d2); mechanical advantage multiplies force while conserving energy.
FLUID-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming hydraulic press creates energy rather than multiplying force through displacement trade-off.

FLUID-04.title: U-Tube Manometry & Immiscible Interfaces
FLUID-04.canonical_rule: In connected communicating vessels, continuous liquid of the same density equilibrates at equal horizontal levels; for immiscible liquids, column heights satisfy rho_1 * h_1 = rho_2 * h_2.
FLUID-04.scope_condition: Static equilibrium in connected open tubes.
FLUID-04.model_check: Equate pressures at the horizontal datum passing through the lowest common interface.
FLUID-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Equating liquid heights directly without weighting by fluid densities.

FLUID-05.title: Archimedes' Law & Buoyant Force Origin
FLUID-05.canonical_rule: Buoyant force F_B = rho_fluid * V_submerged * g originates from the net upward difference of hydrostatic pressures between bottom and top immersed surfaces.
FLUID-05.scope_condition: Immersed bodies in static fluid under gravity.
FLUID-05.model_check: Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid; once completely submerged, F_B is constant and independent of depth in incompressible liquid.
FLUID-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing buoyant force increases as an object sinks deeper into an incompressible liquid.

FLUID-06.title: Floating Equilibrium & Submerged Fraction
FLUID-06.canonical_rule: A floating body equilibrates where its total weight equals buoyant force: rho_body * V_total * g = rho_fluid * V_submerged * g => V_submerged / V_total = rho_body / rho_fluid.
FLUID-06.scope_condition: Free floating body with rho_body <= rho_fluid.
FLUID-06.model_check: The submerged fraction equals the specific gravity ratio rho_body / rho_fluid; melting ice floating in water leaves liquid level unchanged.
FLUID-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Inverting the ratio to V_sub / V_tot = rho_fluid / rho_body.

FLUID-07.title: Apparent Weight & Scale Readings
FLUID-07.canonical_rule: Apparent weight of a submerged body is W_app = W - F_B = (rho_body - rho_fluid) * V * g; normal force reading from a support scale drops by F_B.
FLUID-07.scope_condition: Bodies suspended or resting on scales inside fluid.
FLUID-07.model_check: If rho_body = rho_fluid (neutral buoyancy), apparent weight is identically zero.
FLUID-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming an object loses mass when submerged in liquid.

FLUID-08.title: Newton's Third Law in Buoyancy
FLUID-08.canonical_rule: If a fluid exerts upward buoyant force F_B on an object, the object exerts an equal downward reaction force F_B on the fluid, increasing a base scale reading by exactly F_B.
FLUID-08.scope_condition: Beakers resting on weighing scales containing suspended immersed bodies.
FLUID-08.model_check: Suspended mass decreases tension scale by F_B and increases beaker scale reading by F_B.
FLUID-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming a suspended object exerts no downward force on the beaker containing the fluid.

FLUID-09.title: Accelerating Fluids & Effective Gravity
FLUID-09.canonical_rule: In an accelerating fluid container, the free surface tilts perpendicular to the effective gravity vector g_eff = g - a; surface angle satisfies tan theta = a_x / g.
FLUID-09.scope_condition: Rigid body fluid acceleration without sloshing turbulence.
FLUID-09.model_check: In free-falling fluid (a = g downward), g_eff = 0, so hydrostatic pressure differences and buoyant forces vanish identically.
FLUID-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming buoyant force persists in free fall.

FLUID-10.title: Surface Energy & Capillary Invariants
FLUID-10.canonical_rule: Surface tension gamma = dF/dL = dW/dA produces excess pressure Delta P = 2gamma / R across spherical interfaces and capillary rise h = 2gamma cos theta / (rho g r).
FLUID-10.scope_condition: Narrow cylindrical capillary tubes and curved liquid interfaces.
FLUID-10.model_check: Jurin's law: capillary height is inversely proportional to tube radius (h * r = const).
FLUID-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing excess pressure of a liquid droplet (1 surface: 2gamma/R) with a soap bubble (2 surfaces: 4gamma/R).

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing liquid pressure at the base depends on container shape or total liquid volume rather than vertical depth h.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Hydrostatic pressure P = rho * g * h depends strictly on vertical column depth, completely independent of container geometry or lateral wall slope.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing buoyant force increases as an object sinks deeper into an incompressible liquid.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Buoyant force F_B = rho_fluid * V_submerged * g depends strictly on displaced volume. For an incompressible fluid, F_B is constant once completely submerged.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing buoyant force depends on the mass or density of the submerged body.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced liquid; it depends strictly on fluid density and displaced volume, independent of object material composition.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming a submerged suspended object exerts no downward force on the beaker scale.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: By Newton's 3rd Law, if fluid exerts upward buoyant force F_B on the object, the object exerts an equal downward reaction force F_B on the fluid, increasing beaker scale reading by F_B.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Inverting the submerged fraction ratio of a floating body.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Floating equilibrium requires weight = buoyancy: rho_body * V_total * g = rho_fluid * V_submerged * g => V_submerged / V_total = rho_body / rho_fluid.

heat-thermodynamics.display_name: Heat, Calorimetry & First Law of Thermodynamics

coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: First Law dQ = dU + dW (Work done by expanding gas is positive: dW = P dV). Heat supplied to system is positive (+dQ).
coordinate_conventions.temperature: Absolute thermodynamic temperature in Kelvin: T(K) = T(C) + 273.15. Delta T(K) == Delta T(C).
coordinate_conventions.units: SI (Heat and Work in Joules = kg m^2 s^-2, Specific heat capacity in J kg^-1 K^-1, Latent heat in J kg^-1, Pressure in Pa, Volume in m^3)

svg_specifications: State paths on PV diagrams marked with arrows indicating process direction
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all labels and annotations
Heating curves must clearly show flat plateau regimes for phase transitions at constant temperature
Cyclic loops must indicate clockwise (net positive work engine) vs counterclockwise (refrigerator)

THERMO-01.title: Temperature vs Heat vs Internal Energy
THERMO-01.canonical_rule: Temperature is an intensive state variable measuring average molecular kinetic energy; Heat is thermal energy in transit across a boundary due to Delta T; Internal energy is total molecular state function U.
THERMO-01.model_check: Two bodies in thermal equilibrium have identical temperatures, not necessarily equal heat or internal energy.
THERMO-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Conflating heat Q (energy in transit) with temperature T.

THERMO-02.title: Specific Heat Capacity & Sensible Heat
THERMO-02.canonical_rule: Sensible heat exchange without phase transition is Q = m * c * Delta T; thermal inertia is proportional to heat capacity C = mc.
THERMO-02.scope_condition: Uniform temperature change away from phase transition points.
THERMO-02.model_check: Water has a very high specific heat capacity (4186 J/(kg K)), allowing it to store large amounts of heat with small temperature shifts.
THERMO-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming bodies receiving equal heat experience equal temperature rises regardless of mass and specific heat.

THERMO-03.title: Latent Heat & Phase Transitions
THERMO-03.canonical_rule: During first-order phase transitions (melting, boiling), supplied latent heat Q = m * L breaks intermolecular bonds at strictly constant temperature.
THERMO-03.model_check: On heating curves, phase transitions appear as horizontal plateau lines (Delta T = 0).
THERMO-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming temperature must rise whenever heat is supplied during a phase transition.

THERMO-04.title: Principle of Calorimetry & Water Equivalent
THERMO-04.canonical_rule: In an isolated calorimeter, heat lost by hot bodies equals heat gained by cold bodies: Sigma Q_lost = Sigma Q_gained; container water equivalent W_eq = m_cal * c_cal / c_w must be included.
THERMO-04.model_check: Check whether mixture reaches equilibrium before or after complete phase melting.
THERMO-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Neglecting the heat absorbed by the calorimeter container vessel.

THERMO-05.title: Thermal Expansion in Solids & Liquids
THERMO-05.canonical_rule: Thermal expansion follows Delta L = alpha * L_0 * Delta T, Delta A = 2alpha * A_0 * Delta T, Delta V = 3alpha * V_0 * Delta T; water exhibits anomalous expansion between 0 C and 4 C.
THERMO-05.model_check: Holes in metal plates expand when heated at the exact same fractional rate as if filled with solid metal.
THERMO-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming a central hole in a heated metal ring shrinks.

THERMO-06.title: Modes of Heat Transfer
THERMO-06.canonical_rule: Conduction rate is dQ/dt = k * A * Delta T / L; Convection involves macroscopic fluid flow; Radiation follows Stefan-Boltzmann Law P = epsilon * sigma * A * T^4.
THERMO-06.model_check: Radiation requires no material medium and dominates at high temperatures due to T^4 dependence.
THERMO-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming heat transfer rate depends on mass rather than temperature gradient and surface area.

THERMO-07.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
THERMO-07.canonical_rule: The First Law expresses energy conservation: dQ = dU + dW, where internal energy U is an exact state function (oint dU = 0) while Q and W are path-dependent process quantities.
THERMO-07.model_check: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends solely on temperature: Delta U = n * C_v * Delta T.
THERMO-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Treating heat Q and work W as state functions.

THERMO-08.title: Thermodynamic Work & PV Diagrams
THERMO-08.canonical_rule: Work done by a gas is W = int P dV (area under PV trajectory); work is positive for expansion (dV > 0) and negative for compression (dV < 0).
THERMO-08.model_check: Enclosed area in a cyclic PV diagram represents net work done per cycle; clockwise cycles produce positive net work (engines).
THERMO-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Calculating work without integrating under the specific PV path.

THERMO-09.title: Special Thermodynamic Processes
THERMO-09.canonical_rule: Isochoric (dV = 0 => W = 0, Q = Delta U); Isobaric (W = P Delta V); Isothermal (Delta T = 0 => Delta U = 0, Q = W); Adiabatic (Q = 0 => Delta U = -W, PV^gamma = const).
THERMO-09.scope_condition: Ideal gases undergoing standard quasi-static processes.
THERMO-09.model_check: Adiabatic expansion performs work at the expense of internal energy, causing temperature to fall (Delta T < 0).
THERMO-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing an adiabatic expansion (Q = 0) maintains constant temperature.

THERMO-10.title: Cyclic Engines & Second Law Invariants
THERMO-10.canonical_rule: A heat engine absorbs heat Q_H from hot reservoir, delivers net work W, and exhausts waste heat Q_C to cold sink; thermal efficiency is eta = W / Q_H = 1 - Q_C / Q_H < 1.
THERMO-10.scope_condition: Cyclic heat engines operating between thermal reservoirs.
THERMO-10.model_check: Kelvin-Planck statement: No engine can convert 100% of absorbed heat into work in a complete cycle; Carnot efficiency eta_max = 1 - T_C / T_H sets the thermodynamic ceiling.
THERMO-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming an ideal frictionless engine can achieve 100% thermal efficiency.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Conflating heat Q (energy in transit) with temperature T (average microscopic kinetic energy).
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Heat is energy transferred across a boundary due to temperature difference; temperature is an intensive state variable measuring average particle kinetic energy.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Assuming temperature must rise while heat is supplied during a phase transition (melting/boiling).
misconception_discriminators.refutation: During a first-order phase transition at constant pressure, latent heat is consumed breaking intermolecular bonds while temperature remains strictly constant.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Treating work W and heat Q as state functions that depend only on initial and final states.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: Heat and work are path-dependent process quantities; only internal energy U is an exact state function: oint dU = 0 while cyclic work oint dW = Area under PV curve.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Believing an adiabatic process (Q = 0) must maintain constant temperature.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: By the First Law, Delta U = -W. When a gas expands adiabatically doing positive work on surroundings, its internal energy drops and its temperature falls.

misconception_discriminators.pattern: Neglecting water equivalent of container in calorimetry mixtures.
misconception_discriminators.refutation: The calorimeter vessel absorbs heat: Q_vessel = m_cal * c_cal * Delta T = W_eq * c_water * Delta T, and must be included in heat balance.

coordinate_conventions.system: Standard right-handed Cartesian frame (i_hat, j_hat, k_hat)
coordinate_conventions.axes: x-axis horizontal positive right / east; y-axis vertical positive up / north; z-axis out of page
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Sign encodes orientation relative to declared positive axis; negative indicates antiparallel direction, not smaller magnitude
coordinate_conventions.units: SI derived units (arbitrary vector magnitude, angles in radians and degrees)

svg_specifications: Vectors represented as sharp directed arrows with arrowheads terminating exactly at target coordinates
Component projections indicated by dashed orthogonal projection lines with right-angle indicators
Minimum SVG text font floor >= 14px on all vector magnitude, component, and angle annotations

dimensional_signatures.vector_magnitude: Inherits base or derived physical dimension [L], [L T^-1], [M L T^-2], etc.

VEC-01.title: Scalars, Vectors & Signed Axis Conventions
VEC-01.canonical_rule: A scalar is fully characterized by magnitude alone; a vector requires magnitude and spatial direction. In 1D, sign indicates orientation along a declared axis; negative means antiparallel, not smaller.
VEC-01.model_check: Reversing the declared coordinate axis flips component signs without altering physical state.
VEC-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Treating negative vector components as smaller magnitudes rather than opposite directions.

VEC-02.title: Vector Equality, Opposite Vectors & Null Vector
VEC-02.canonical_rule: Two vectors are equal if and only if both magnitude and direction match identically, regardless of origin; opposite vector -A has identical magnitude and reversed direction; A + (-A) = 0.
VEC-02.model_check: Parallel translation in space preserves vector identity.
VEC-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Judging vector equality solely by arrow length while ignoring spatial direction.

VEC-03.title: Orthogonal Components, Quadrants & Angle References
VEC-03.canonical_rule: A 2D vector A resolves into rectangular components A_x = A cos theta and A_y = A sin theta where theta is measured from the adjacent axis; quadrant determines component algebraic signs.
VEC-03.model_check: A_x^2 + A_y^2 = A^2 regardless of chosen coordinate frame orientation.
VEC-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Memorizing cos theta always belongs to x-axis, failing when angle is referenced to vertical.

VEC-04.title: Vector Addition, Triangle & Parallelogram Laws, Resultant
VEC-04.canonical_rule: Vector sum R = A + B is constructed geometrically by head-to-tail placement or diagonal of parallelogram; algebraically R_x = A_x + B_x and R_y = A_y + B_y; |A - B| <= R <= A + B.
VEC-04.model_check: Resultant magnitude R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + 2AB cos theta).
VEC-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Adding vector magnitudes algebraically without vector decomposition.

VEC-05.title: Vector Subtraction & Change Vectors
VEC-05.canonical_rule: Vector subtraction A - B equals adding the additive inverse: A + (-B); change in velocity Delta v = v_f - v_i points from initial velocity vector tip to final velocity vector tip when co-initial.
VEC-05.model_check: Constant speed v turning through angle theta experiences Delta v = 2v sin(theta/2) != 0.
VEC-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming change in velocity is zero when speed remains constant along a curved path.

VEC-06.title: Magnitude & Direction Angle Recovery
VEC-06.canonical_rule: Given Cartesian components (A_x, A_y), vector magnitude is A = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2) and orientation angle is recovered via tan phi = |A_y / A_x| with quadrant placed by signs of A_x and A_y.
VEC-06.model_check: Inverse tangent yields reference angle only; true azimuth requires Cartesian quadrant disambiguation.
VEC-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Accepting raw calculator arctan output without adjusting for quadrant.

VEC-07.title: Relative Velocity in 1D & 2D Frames
VEC-07.canonical_rule: Velocity of body A relative to observer B is v_AB = v_A - v_B; to observe from frame B, subtract vector v_B from all tracked objects: v_AB = -v_BA.
VEC-07.model_check: Two objects approaching along a straight line have relative approach speed v_1 + v_2.
VEC-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Reversing subtraction order or adding frame velocity instead of subtracting it.

VEC-08.title: Radial & Tangential Decomposition in Curvilinear Paths
VEC-08.canonical_rule: Curvilinear acceleration decomposes into tangential acceleration a_t = dv/dt (rate of change of speed) along tangent, and centripetal acceleration a_r = v^2/R directed toward instantaneous center of curvature.
VEC-08.model_check: Total acceleration magnitude is a_net = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_r^2); for uniform circular motion a_t = 0.
VEC-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Drawing release or instantaneous velocity radially outward due to centrifugal fallacy.

VEC-09.title: Component Ownership & Inclined Plane Decomposition
VEC-09.canonical_rule: Gravity weight W = mg acts strictly vertically downward; along an incline of angle theta, weight decomposes into mg sin theta parallel to incline and mg cos theta perpendicular to incline.
VEC-09.model_check: Normal contact force balances perpendicular component N = mg cos theta; net driving force is mg sin theta - f_k.
VEC-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Conflating incline angle theta with complement, swapping sine and cosine components.

VEC-10.title: Scalar (Dot) Product, Projection & Work Mechanics
VEC-10.canonical_rule: Dot product A . B = |A||B| cos theta evaluates scalar projection of A along B; work W = F . d = F d cos theta is positive for acute angles, zero for perpendicular forces, and negative for obtuse angles.
VEC-10.model_check: A . B = A_x B_x + A_y B_y; orthogonal vectors have A . B = 0.
VEC-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Assigning a direction to a scalar dot product or failing to check sign from cosine.

VEC-11.title: Vector (Cross) Product, Torque & Planar Orthogonal Invariants
VEC-11.canonical_rule: Vector cross product C = A x B has magnitude |A||B| sin theta and direction normal to A-B plane via right-hand screw rule; torque tau = r x F; bridge to planar kinematics where independent perpendicular axes decouple.
VEC-11.scope_condition: 3D rotational mechanics and planar vector decoupling.
VEC-11.model_check: Cross product is antisymmetric: B x A = -(A x B); parallel vectors have zero cross product.
VEC-11.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming cross product is commutative (A x B = B x A).

misconception_discriminators.label: Scalar Addition of Vector Magnitudes
misconception_discriminators.description: Adding vector magnitudes directly (|A + B| = A + B) regardless of angle between vectors.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Apply parallelogram formula R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + 2AB cos theta) or sum rectangular components algebraically.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: direct arithmetic sum of lengths without direction cosine

misconception_discriminators.label: Sign-Magnitude Confusion
misconception_discriminators.description: Interpreting negative component sign as smaller physical magnitude rather than opposite direction along chosen axis.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Separate magnitude (strictly non-negative absolute value) from orientation sign (+/- indicates axis direction).
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: treating -5 m/s as slower than +2 m/s

misconception_discriminators.label: Angle-Reference Axis Inversion
misconception_discriminators.description: Rote application of cos theta to horizontal and sin theta to vertical regardless of specified reference axis.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Identify adjacent axis to angle theta for cosine projection; opposite side receives sine projection.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: blind cos(theta) along x-axis when angle is given relative to vertical

misconception_discriminators.label: Vector Subtraction Order Reversal
misconception_discriminators.description: Reversing subtraction vector order: constructing B - A instead of Delta v = v_f - v_i.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Change vector Delta A = A_final - A_initial; arrow points from initial tip to final tip.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: drawing change vector pointing towards initial state

misconception_discriminators.label: Relative Frame Sign Inversion
misconception_discriminators.description: Adding frame observer velocity rather than subtracting it: v_AB = v_A + v_B instead of v_A - v_B.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: To bring observer B to rest, apply equal and opposite velocity -v_B to all entities.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: conflating relative velocity with combined closing speed

misconception_discriminators.label: Dot vs Cross Product Misapplication
misconception_discriminators.description: Confusing scalar projection (dot product) with vector normal generation (cross product) or treating dot product as vector.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Dot product produces scalar work W = F . d; Cross product produces perpendicular pseudovector torque tau = r x F.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: assigning direction to work or treating torque as scalar projection

motion-in-a-plane.display_name: Motion in a Plane: Projectiles, Relative Frames & Curvilinear Motion

coordinate_conventions.system: 2D Cartesian plane (x: horizontal range, y: vertical height)
coordinate_conventions.axes: x horizontal positive in launch direction; y vertical positive upward; origin at launch point or ground datum
coordinate_conventions.sign_convention: Downward gravity acceleration a_y = -g; horizontal acceleration a_x = 0 (ideal unresisted flight)
coordinate_conventions.units: SI units (m, m/s, m/s^2, s, rad/deg)

svg_specifications: Parabolic path rendered with apex landmark (v_y = 0) and ground landing coordinates
Horizontal velocity vector u_x kept strictly constant across all trajectory points
Minimum font floor >= 14px on all kinematic labels, velocity components, and angles

PLANE-01.title: 2D Position & Velocity Component Independence
PLANE-01.canonical_rule: Motion in a plane decomposes into two mutually perpendicular 1D motions that evolve independently under a shared universal time parameter t: r(t) = x(t) i_hat + y(t) j_hat.
PLANE-01.model_check: Gravity acting purely along the y-axis has zero effect on horizontal velocity component: a_x = 0 => v_x(t) = u_x.
PLANE-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing gravity slows down horizontal motion of a projectile.

PLANE-02.title: Constant-Acceleration Equations in Vector Form
PLANE-02.canonical_rule: For uniform acceleration a, displacement Delta r = u t + (1/2) a t^2 and velocity v = u + a t hold component-wise: x = u_x t, y = u_y t - (1/2) g t^2.
PLANE-02.scope_condition: Constant uniform field without aerodynamic drag.
PLANE-02.model_check: At any instant, speed is v = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) and velocity direction angle is phi = arctan(v_y / v_x).
PLANE-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Attempting to combine x and y displacements into a single scalar before squaring.

PLANE-03.title: Horizontal Launch from Elevated Height
PLANE-03.canonical_rule: In horizontal launch from height h with initial velocity u, u_y = 0; fall time t_f = sqrt(2h/g) depends purely on height; horizontal landing range is x = u sqrt(2h/g).
PLANE-03.model_check: Dropping a ball vertically and projecting a ball horizontally from identical height results in simultaneous ground impact.
PLANE-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Thinking greater horizontal launch speed prolongs the fall time.

PLANE-04.title: Ground-to-Ground Oblique Projectile Flight Time & Apex
PLANE-04.canonical_rule: For launch at angle theta with speed u: time of flight is T = 2 u sin theta / g; maximum apex height is H = u^2 sin^2 theta / (2g); at the apex, vertical velocity vanishes v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity remains v_x = u cos theta.
PLANE-04.model_check: At the top of trajectory, speed reaches its global minimum v_min = u cos theta > 0.
PLANE-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming total speed is zero at the apex of projectile flight.

PLANE-05.title: Horizontal Range & Maximum Range Invariant
PLANE-05.canonical_rule: Horizontal range R = u^2 sin(2 theta) / g; for a given launch speed u, maximum range R_max = u^2 / g occurs at theta = 45 degrees, where H_max = R_max / 4.
PLANE-05.model_check: Ratio of range to maximum height is R / H = 4 cot theta.
PLANE-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming maximum height occurs at 45 degrees launch angle.

PLANE-06.title: Complementary Launch Angles & Trajectory Envelopes
PLANE-06.canonical_rule: Launch angles theta and (90 - theta) yield identical horizontal ranges R, because sin(2(90 - theta)) = sin(180 - 2 theta) = sin(2 theta); higher angle has longer flight time and greater apex.
PLANE-06.model_check: Product of flight times for complementary angles is T_1 T_2 = 2 R / g.
PLANE-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming equal range implies equal flight times or equal apex heights.

PLANE-07.title: Cartesian Trajectory Parabola Equation
PLANE-07.canonical_rule: Eliminating time t gives parabolic trajectory y(x) = x tan theta - g x^2 / (2 u^2 cos^2 theta) = x tan theta [1 - x / R].
PLANE-07.model_check: Roots of y(x) = 0 occur at launch x = 0 and landing x = R.
PLANE-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Treating trajectory equation as linear or failing to convert 1/cos^2 theta to (1 + tan^2 theta).

PLANE-08.title: Relative Velocity: River-Boat Shortest Time vs Zero Drift
PLANE-08.canonical_rule: Boat ground velocity is v_b = v_bw + v_w; crossing time t = d / v_y is minimized (t_min = d / v_bw) when boat heads directly perpendicular to banks; zero drift requires heading upstream with sin theta = v_w / v_bw (requires v_bw > v_w).
PLANE-08.scope_condition: Crossing flowing stream of width d and water speed v_w.
PLANE-08.model_check: Crossing time in minimum-time route is completely independent of stream speed v_w.
PLANE-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing shortest time route with shortest distance (zero drift) route.

PLANE-09.title: Relative Velocity: Rain-Man & Aircraft Wind Drift
PLANE-09.canonical_rule: Apparent rain velocity seen by moving person is v_rain/person = v_rain - v_person; umbrella must be aligned parallel to v_rain/person: tan theta = v_person / v_rain from vertical.
PLANE-09.model_check: If rain falls vertically and person moves east, relative rain arrives from east, requiring forward umbrella tilt.
PLANE-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Tilting umbrella backwards away from direction of motion.

PLANE-10.title: Uniform Circular Motion: Centripetal Acceleration Invariant
PLANE-10.canonical_rule: In uniform circular motion with constant speed v and radius R, velocity direction changes continuously; acceleration is purely centripetal a_c = v^2 / R = omega^2 R directed radially toward center.
PLANE-10.scope_condition: Planar circular trajectory with constant speed.
PLANE-10.model_check: Speed is constant but acceleration is non-zero because velocity vector rotates at rate omega.
PLANE-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Asserting that constant speed implies zero acceleration in circular motion.

PLANE-11.title: Non-Uniform Curvilinear Motion: Tangential vs Normal Components
PLANE-11.canonical_rule: In non-uniform planar motion, total acceleration a = a_t t_hat + a_c n_hat where tangential acceleration a_t = dv/dt changes speed and normal acceleration a_c = v^2/rho changes direction; a_net = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_c^2).
PLANE-11.scope_condition: General curvilinear trajectories with local radius of curvature rho.
PLANE-11.model_check: When particle speeds up, a_t is parallel to v; when slowing down, a_t is antiparallel to v.
PLANE-11.easy_mistake_to_make: Equating total acceleration magnitude directly to centripetal acceleration.

misconception_discriminators.label: Apex Velocity Vanishing Fallacy
misconception_discriminators.description: Believing that a projectile launched at an angle stops completely at the top of its trajectory.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: At the apex, only vertical velocity component vanishes (v_y = 0); horizontal velocity persists (v_x = u cos theta).

misconception_discriminators.label: Gravity-Horizontal Velocity Coupling Fallacy
misconception_discriminators.description: Assuming that downward gravity reduces or retards horizontal projectile speed.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Perpendicular vectors are decoupled: a_x = 0 throughout unresisted flight.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: introducing deceleration into horizontal motion equation

misconception_discriminators.label: Horizontal Launch Drop Time Fallacy
misconception_discriminators.description: Believing that a horizontally fired projectile takes longer to hit the ground than a dropped object.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Vertical free-fall equation y = (1/2) g t^2 governs both identically: t = sqrt(2h/g).
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: claiming horizontal speed delays downward impact

misconception_discriminators.label: River Crossing Minimum Time vs Zero Drift Conflation
misconception_discriminators.description: Conflating shortest crossing time with shortest crossing distance across a river.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Shortest time requires aiming directly across (perpendicular); shortest distance requires angling upstream to cancel drift.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: asserting zero drift path has minimum crossing time

misconception_discriminators.label: Rain-Man Umbrella Tilt Inversion
misconception_discriminators.description: Tilting umbrella backwards or incorrectly calculating angle relative to horizontal instead of vertical.
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Relative rain velocity is v_r - v_m; if runner moves forward, rain appears to blow toward them, requiring forward tilt.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: inverting tangent ratio or tilting umbrella away from relative wind

misconception_discriminators.label: Centripetal vs Tangential Acceleration Conflation
misconception_discriminators.description: Confusing rate of change of speed (dv/dt) with rate of change of direction (v^2/R).
misconception_discriminators.remedy: Tangential acceleration a_t = dv/dt is collinear with velocity; normal acceleration a_n = v^2/R is strictly perpendicular.
misconception_discriminators.trigger_pattern: setting centripetal acceleration to zero because speed is constant
